notes_list.title: Chirality and Elements of Symmetry
notes_list.basic_overview: A molecule is chiral when it is not superposable on its mirror image. Symmetry analysis helps identify whether a structure can be achiral.
notes_list.extra_info_content: Common symmetry elements: proper rotation axis Cn, mirror plane σ, inversion center i, and improper rotation axis Sn. A molecule containing a mirror plane, inversion center or Sn operation is achiral.
notes_list.examples: 2-butanol is chiral at C2. Meso compounds contain stereocenters but are achiral because of internal symmetry.
notes_list.conditions_and_medium: No reaction conditions; chirality is a structural property. Reactions can create, destroy or transfer stereochemical information.
notes_list.mechanism_steps: 1. Identify stereogenic elements. 2. Search for symmetry. 3. Generate mirror image. 4. Test superposability. 5. Assign configurations if required.
notes_list.kinetics_and_energy: Stereochemical purity can be measured using enantiomeric excess. Racemization occurs when a planar achiral intermediate allows attack from either face.
notes_list.selectivity_and_stereochemistry: Core for SN1 racemization, asymmetric synthesis, spectroscopy and conformational analysis.
notes_list.common_traps: A carbon with four different substituents is a common stereocenter but is not the only source of chirality.

exam_focus.level: IIT-JAM / MSc entrance / GATE concept depth
